assumptions: Illustrative synthetic layout; not surveyed Taman Kyra underground assets.
Coordinates use an arbitrary local metric datum; they are not latitude/longitude.
Node positions are pipe inverts; inlet positions are surface grate elevations.
Diameters, roughness, elevations and grate areas are synthetic demonstration inputs, not verified site design values.
Independent inlet capture and obstruction modelling are not yet implemented; the T1 clean baseline routes runoff directly to sewer nodes.
No surface terrain coupling or validated street flood depths are available.
Four synthetic 1 ha catchments, each 80% impervious; areas do not imply surveyed catchment boundaries.
Surface routing uses the SWMM nonlinear reservoir with synthetic width, slope, roughness and depression storage; infiltration uses assumed Horton parameters.
Outfall stage is fixed at invert plus the selected assumed tailwater depth; no observed river hydrograph is available.
One-hour rain is followed by one-hour dry drainage; the full simulation window is included in metrics.

T3 uses native SWMM CUSTOM DIVERSION inlet capture in four independent illustrative open rectangular approach channels. The assumed curve captures 80% of approach flow up to 0.20 m3/s, before applying clogging.

Each catchment drains to its mapped auxiliary surface approach node. Captured flow enters the original sewer node; non-captured flow passes a separate bypass junction and exit conduit to a free surface outfall. Sewer overflow can return through the native inlet backflow mechanism.
Auxiliary channels are numerical sensitivity elements, not surveyed roads, pipes, mapped assets, or a 2D street-flood model. Their geometry and rating curve are uncalibrated assumptions.

Only the selected inlet receives the independent constant hydraulic capacity-loss fraction; other inlets use zero loss with the same finite capture curve. Original sewer conduit diameters and Manning n are unchanged.
Compare finite-capture scenarios against finite 0% capture loss with identical storm and boundary. The retained T1/T2 unlimited direct-node clean baseline is a different capture assumption.

Surface bypass volume is discharged outside this illustrative domain; it is not a computed street inundation depth or automatically added to sewer flooding volume. Greater restriction can reduce sewer flooding while increasing bypass.
warnings: Trace native flooding <0.1 m3 at NODE-J01, NODE-J02, NODE-J03; tiny transient events and flooded-node counts can be sensitive to routing settings. Volumes/counts are retained without filtering.
Finite uncalibrated inlet capture: compare with finite 0% using identical storm/boundary. Reduced sewer flooding can accompany increased surface bypass; display inlet_volumes separately.

status_definitions.node_surcharged: Junction depth + 0.00003048 m >= highest connected conduit crown above its invert; outfall excluded. Matches SWMM crown criterion for this zero-offset, circular-conduit model.
status_definitions.node_flooding: Reported node flooding loss rate > 1e-9 m3/s; takes display precedence over surcharge. Not a surface flood depth.
status_definitions.node_normal: Neither flooding nor crown exceedance at this report instant; outfall is not classified as surcharged.
status_definitions.pipe_surcharged: Hydraulic heads at both endpoints exceed their respective conduit crown elevations by > 0.00003048 m; indicates pressurized closed conduit at both ends.
status_definitions.pipe_near_capacity: Not surcharged by the endpoint-head rule and reported conduit depth/diameter >= 0.8; a geometric fullness display threshold, not a discharge-capacity or failure estimate.
status_definitions.pipe_normal: Neither endpoint-head surcharge nor depth/diameter >= 0.8 at this report instant.
status_definitions.unknown: Missing or unsupported hydraulic information; never inferred from inlet restriction.
status_definitions.inlet: Independent assumed hydraulic_inlet_clogging_fraction=0; T1 uses unlimited direct-node runoff entry, not a finite-capacity inlet or calibrated capture model.
